Customer.title: Customer
Customer.description: Represents a customer who applies for a credit in Tecnicell Créditos.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Customer entity.

phoneNumber.description: The customer's phone number, including country code if applicable.

identificationNumber.description: The customer's national identification number (e.g., DNI, Passport).

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the customer record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the customer record was last updated.

Credit.title: Credit
Credit.description: Represents a credit application for a customer, including loan terms and overall status.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Credit entity.

customerId.description: Reference to the Customer who owns this credit. (Relationship: Customer 1:N Credit)

initialAmount.description: The original principal amount of the loan requested.

totalAmountCharged.description: The total amount the customer is required to pay, including the initial amount and the markup.

markupPercentage.description: The percentage applied to the initial amount (50% or 100%) to calculate the total amount charged.

installmentsPlanType.description: The type of installment plan chosen by the customer (e.g., 6 bi-weekly, 12 bi-weekly).

totalInstallments.description: The total number of installments for this credit (e.g., 6 or 12).

startDate.description: The date when the credit was approved and started.

status.description: The current status of the credit (e.g., Active, Paid, Overdue, Cancelled).

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the credit record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the credit record was last updated.

Installment.title: Installment
Installment.description: Represents a single scheduled payment (installment) for a credit, including its due date and payment status.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Installment entity.

creditId.description: Reference to the Credit this installment belongs to. (Relationship: Credit 1:N Installment)

installmentNumber.description: The sequential number of the installment within its credit (e.g., 1, 2, 3).

dueDate.description: The date by which this installment is expected to be paid.

expectedAmount.description: The full amount expected to be paid for this installment.

paidAmount.description: The total amount that has been paid towards this specific installment so far.

status.description: The current payment status of the installment (e.g., Pending, Paid, Partially Paid, Overdue).

balanceRemaining.description: The amount still owed for this specific installment (expectedAmount - paidAmount).

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the installment record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the installment record was last updated.

Payment.title: Payment
Payment.description: Records an individual payment made by a customer towards a specific credit.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Payment entity.

creditId.description: Reference to the Credit this payment applies to. (Relationship: Credit 1:N Payment)

amount.description: The amount of this specific payment transaction.

paymentDate.description: The date and time when the payment was made.

paymentMethod.description: The method used for this payment (e.g., Cash, Bank Transfer, Card).

notes.description: Any additional notes or details about the payment.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the payment record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the payment record was last updated.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure for Tecnicell Créditos is designed to be secure, scalable, and debuggable, adhering to the core design principles. This structure primarily supports an internal staff-facing application where authenticated staff members manage customer credits.

1.  **Staff Authorization (DBAC):** For robust Database Access Control (DBAC), a dedicated top-level collection, `/staffRoles/{staffUid}`, will be used. The *existence* of a document at `/staffRoles/$(request.auth.uid)` signifies that the authenticated user (`request.auth.uid`) is an authorized staff member. This approach prevents reliance on custom claims, simplifies security rules by centralizing role checks, and makes authorization intent explicit. Any authenticated staff member will have full read/write access to all customer and credit-related data.

2.  **Hierarchical and Segregated Data (Clarity & QAPs):**
    *   **`/customers/{customerId}`:** This is the foundational collection, storing individual `Customer` profiles. Each document represents a customer of Tecnicell Créditos. Access to this collection, and all its subcollections, is restricted to authorized staff, ensuring a homogeneous security posture.
    *   **`/customers/{customerId}/credits/{creditId}`:** This subcollection holds individual `Credit` applications for a specific customer. This path-based ownership makes the relationship between a customer and their credits clear and simplifies security rules for credit access.
    *   **`/customers/{customerId}/credits/{creditId}/installments/{installmentId}`:** This nested subcollection stores the scheduled `Installment` payments pertaining to a specific `Credit`. Continuing the hierarchy naturally segments the data.
    *   **`/customers/{customerId}/credits/{creditId}/payments/{paymentId}`:** This subcollection records all individual `Payment` transactions made towards a particular `Credit`.

3.  **Authorization Independence via Denormalization (CRITICAL):** To eliminate the need for expensive and complex `get()` calls to parent documents within security rules, and to enable atomic operations, authorization context is denormalized where necessary:
    *   Each `Credit` document includes its `customerId`, which is already part of its schema, providing direct parent reference.
    *   Every `Installment` document (located under `/customers/{customerId}/credits/{creditId}/installments/{installmentId}`) will be denormalized to include its `customerId` (in addition to its `creditId` already in the schema). This ensures that rules evaluating an `Installment` can directly verify its association with the `Customer` and `Credit` without fetching ancestor documents.
    *   Similarly, every `Payment` document (located under `/customers/{customerId}/credits/{creditId}/payments/{paymentId}`) will include its `customerId` (in addition to its `creditId` already in the schema). This again provides immediate access to the necessary authorization context, enhancing rule efficiency and debuggability.

4.  **QAPs (Query Access Patterns) Support:** The structured segregation of data and consistent security posture within each collection naturally supports Query Access Patterns. Staff members can perform efficient `list` operations (e.g., retrieving all customers, all credits for a customer, or all installments for a credit) without security rules acting as filters. The global staff authorization check ensures that `list` operations return only data permitted by the top-level staff role, preventing incomplete results and ensuring performance.

5.  **Data Clarity and Predictability:** The design uses descriptive wildcards (`{customerId}`, `{creditId}`, etc.), a dedicated `status` field for explicit state modeling in `Credit` and `Installment`, and enforces strict, semantic naming conventions. This consistency enhances the predictability and maintainability of the data structure and associated security rules.
